messages:
Marisol: FYI AcmePayments (tenant-acme) on Dedicated reported a sharp spike of 429s + increased latency for ~10m. They say most requests were routed to the fallback pool instead of their dedicated pool. I have request IDs and a short log clip below.

Devon: Got it — can you drop a sample request id and any headers you see? Also: any autoscaler events around that time?

Marisol: sample req id: req_0a3f2b9f, headers we see in the capture: 
  X-Redwood-Pin: tenant-acme
  X-Redwood-Cost-Tier: low
stack log excerpt: 
  [2026-11-12T14:01:22Z] route-eval: req=req_0a3f2b9f tenant=tenant-acme -> pool=fallback-pool reason=rule(cost_low) matched before rule(pin_owner)
  [2026-11-12T14:01:22Z] controlplane: throttle applied: 429 quota_exceeded on pool=fallback-pool

Ravi: That route-eval line is unusual. I rolled a change yesterday that reorders rule evaluation to optimize cost rules early (memory-savings for hot routes). If cost_low is evaluated before pin_owner, we can get a priority inversion which explains wrong-pool selection.

Devon: Can you repro quickly in staging? If so we can roll back the route-ordering change.

Marisol: Repro steps I used (staging) — sending with both headers toggles the behavior: 
```
# repro curl simulating SDK headers
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." \ 
     -H "X-Redwood-Pin: tenant-acme" \ 
     -H "X-Redwood-Cost-Tier: low" \ 
     -d '{"input":"hello"}' \ 
     https://staging-inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response (staging after change): 200 from fallback-pool with slower latencies.

When I flip order of headers (remove cost header) the request goes to tenant-acme pool as expected.

Ravi: Ok I can reproduce locally with the same headers. The new evaluator sorts rules by a derived score; looks like we accidentally used a comparator that gives cost rules higher precedence for older tenants. That's the priority inversion.

Anya: Acme is on a support call right now and is very worried. They see billing implications and errors. Please escalate. :eyes:

Devon: Escalating to P1. Immediate mitigation options: 1) create a route override pin for tenant-acme in the control plane UI (quick but manual), 2) rollback the route-ordering change (safer), 3) hotfix to add explicit "pin_owner" pre-check. Thoughts?

Ravi: I'll push a rollback for the reorder; also prepare a hotfix branch for an explicit pre-check. Rolling back now.

router-bot: deploy: rollback started: controlplane-routing v1.12.3 -> v1.12.2 (initiated by Ravi). Canary region: us-west-2.

Devon: Monitoring metrics: error-rate for tenant-acme down from 18% -> 1.6% in the last 3 minutes after rollback canary. Latency returned to baseline.

Marisol: Customer confirmed errors dropped and requests are hitting their dedicated pool. They've been patched but want a postmortem and a billing credit ask.

Ravi: I'll open a postmortem and include repro steps, the faulty comparator snippet, and a remediation plan (routing rule unit tests + explicit pre-check).

Anya: I'll handle the customer comms and coordinate billing credit ask.

Devon: Action items: 
- Ravi: postmortem + hotfix PR (ETA 4h)
- Anya: customer comms + temporary credit talk
- Marisol: collect additional request ids for audit

Marisol: Thanks all — marking this thread until postmortem done. :white_check_mark:
